title: Systematic Review of the Accuracy of Large Language Models for Title and Abstract Screening Compared with Human Reviewers
research_question: How accurate are large language models at title and abstract screening for systematic reviews, compared with human reviewers?
rationale: Automated screening promises to reduce workload in systematic reviews, yet the performance of large language models (LLMs) for title and abstract screening remains uncertain. Existing studies report heterogeneous accuracy metrics and methodological quality, making it difficult for reviewers to adopt LLMs confidently. A systematic synthesis of comparative evidence will clarify the current state of LLM screening performance and identify gaps for future research.
objectives: To identify and summarise primary research that evaluates the performance of LLMs for title and abstract screening in systematic reviews.
To compare LLM screening accuracy with that of human reviewers using standard performance measures (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1).
To assess the methodological quality of included studies and explore factors influencing LLM performance.

framework_elements.Population: Records (titles and abstracts) retrieved for systematic review screening
framework_elements.Intervention: Screening performed by a large language model (e.g., GPT‑4, Claude, LLaMA)
framework_elements.Comparator: Screening performed by human reviewers (single or dual independent screening)
framework_elements.Outcome: Accuracy metrics of screening decisions (sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1, area under the ROC curve)

inclusion_criteria.text: Primary research that evaluates a large language model for title and/or abstract screening of systematic review records.
The study reports a quantitative comparison between the LLM and at least one human reviewer or a human reference standard.
The population consists of records retrieved for any health‑related systematic review (any clinical, public‑health or health‑services topic).
The article is written in English.
The study provides at least one accuracy measure (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1, AUC).
Full text is available for data extraction.

exclusion_criteria.text: Not a primary research report (editorials, commentaries, letters, protocols, narrative or systematic reviews).
Studies that evaluate LLMs for tasks other than title/abstract screening (e.g., full‑text retrieval, data extraction, risk‑of‑bias assessment).
Studies that use only simulated data without real systematic‑review records.
Conference abstracts without a full‑text manuscript.
Studies that do not provide a human comparator or reference standard for screening decisions.

study_designs: Randomised controlled trial of screening methods
data_items: Population description (type of systematic review, number of records screened)
Accuracy metrics reported (sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1, AUC)
risk_of_bias_approach: Diagnostic accuracy studies will be appraised with QUADAS‑2; non‑randomised comparative designs will be assessed using ROBINS‑I; any randomised trials of screening methods will be evaluated with RoB 2. Two reviewers will independently apply the tools, with disagreements resolved by consensus.
synthesis_plan: A narrative synthesis will summarise study characteristics, LLM configurations, and reported accuracy metrics, grouped by LLM type and screening workflow. Where at least three studies report the same metric on comparable populations, a random‑effects meta‑analysis of sensitivity and specificity will be performed using a bivariate model; otherwise, results will be presented descriptively.
